headline: Lamine Yamal joins Pele in elite World Cup record books
summary: The 18-year-old Spanish forward became only the second player aged 18 or younger to score the opening goal of a World Cup match.
details: Spanish forward Lamine Yamal etched his name into football history during Spain's match against Saudi Arabia in Atlanta.
The Barcelona star put Spain ahead in the 10th minute, steering in a superb pass from Mikel Oyarzabal.
At 18 years and 343 days old, Yamal became only the second player aged 18 or younger to score the opening goal of a World Cup match in the tournament's 96-year history.
He joins Brazilian legend Pele, who was 17 years and 239 days old when he scored Brazil's only goal against Wales in the 1958 World Cup quarter-finals.
While Pele remains the youngest goalscorer in World Cup history, Yamal now ranks eighth on the list of the youngest World Cup goalscorers overall.
Among Spanish players, only Gavi scored at a younger age, netting at 18 years and 110 days during the 2022 tournament against Costa Rica.
caption:
Only two players in 96 years of World Cup history have done this. Lamine Yamal just joined Pele in the record books.

Spanish forward Lamine Yamal etched his name into football history during Spain's match against Saudi Arabia in Atlanta.

The Barcelona star put Spain ahead in the 10th minute, steering in a superb pass from Mikel Oyarzabal.

At 18 years and 343 days old, Yamal became only the second player aged 18 or younger to score the opening goal of a World Cup match in the tournament's 96-year history.

He joins Brazilian legend Pele, who was 17 years and 239 days old when he scored Brazil's only goal against Wales in the 1958 World Cup quarter-finals.

While Pele remains the youngest goalscorer in World Cup history, Yamal now ranks eighth on the list of the youngest World Cup goalscorers overall.

Among Spanish players, only Gavi scored at a younger age, netting at 18 years and 110 days during the 2022 tournament against Costa Rica.

headline: PM Tarique in Malaysia: Urges expats to focus on serving country over personal demands
summary: During a meeting with the Bangladeshi diaspora in Kuala Lumpur, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman called for a shift from individual demands to national responsibility.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has urged expatriate Bangladeshis in Malaysia to prioritize their responsibilities toward the country over their own personal demands.

Speaking at a meeting with the Bangladeshi diaspora at the Shangri-La Hotel in Kuala Lumpur on Sunday, the PM stated, "Let us move beyond thinking about what our demands are. Let us think about what our responsibilities are towards the country."
The Prime Minister arrived in the Malaysian capital for a two-day official visit around 8:45 PM local time on Sunday, where he was received with a red carpet welcome and a guard of honour.
Accompanied by his wife Zubaida Rahman, he outlined his vision for Bangladesh, including the BNP's election pledges such as the Family Card and Farmer Card schemes.
He also discussed initiatives for canal re-excavation as part of his plans for the nation's development.
caption:

The Prime Minister arrived in the Malaysian capital for a two-day official visit around 8:45 PM local time on Sunday, where he was received with a red carpet welcome and a guard of honour.

Accompanied by his wife Zubaida Rahman, he outlined his vision for Bangladesh, including the BNP's election pledges such as the Family Card and Farmer Card schemes.

He also discussed initiatives for canal re-excavation as part of his plans for the nation's development.
